title: Contour model
description: A Contour specification in the framework's structured-record style (Section 3) with a nested ownership hierarchy: Components nest under their System (groups), and the elements a Component owns — interfaces, functions, dataObjects, events — nest under that Component. Each Interface serves one caller (an Actor, or `Components`) and exposes the Component's Functions with their operation, request and responses. Actors are top-level. Requirement and Guardrail definitions (Section 3.6) are top-level and referenced by name. Cross-boundary edges (groups, uses, consumes, references, dependsOn) and Function steps are inline by name. No IDs. Field names are camelCase.

System.description: The business-capability grouping and root of the ownership tree. A model has at most one System in this style; given as a single element or a one-item list.

Actor.description: An external role with distinct access (Section 3). Top-level because it sits outside the Component boundary. Which Interfaces it uses is derived from the Interfaces that serve it. Given as a single element or a list.

Requirement.description: Record-tier Requirement definitions (Section 3.6), referenced by name from the requirements list of the elements they apply to.

Guardrail.description: Record-tier Guardrail definitions (Section 3.6), referenced by name from the guardrails list of the elements they bound.

name.description: Plain-language element name (Section 3.5); the stable identifier other elements reference by.

description.description: Required plain-language sentence or two — what this element is (Section 3.3).

nameList.description: A list of element or definition names referenced inline.

requirements.description: Names of Requirement definitions this element must satisfy (Section 3.6).

guardrails.description: Names of Guardrail definitions this element must stay inside (Section 3.6).

shape.description: A shape in the core type notation (Section 3.3): a type expression such as "uuid", "string?", "Order.Line Item[1..]", "enum(a, b)" or "Order { id, status }", or an inline mapping of field names to shapes.

schemaField.description: The shape of a Data Object's fields or an Event's payload (Section 3.3): an inline shape in the core type notation, or a string link to an existing spec (AsyncAPI/JSON Schema/Avro).

firstStep.description: The first entry of a Function's steps. Besides an ordinary step it may be `consumes`, naming an Event another Component produces — the Function is started by that Event (Section 3.4).

step.description: One entry of a Function's steps (Section 3.3): exactly one step verb naming its target, plus `becomes` on a `calls` or `uses` step.

calls.description: A Function of the same Component.

uses.description: A Function of another Component, as "Interface / Function" — the Interface must serve `Components` and expose the target.

reads.description: A Data Object of the same Component.

modifies.description: A Data Object of the same Component.

produces.description: An Event of the same Component.

becomes.description: Maps the callee's outcomes to this Function's alternatives (Section 3.3). An outcome that doesn't become anything continues the main path. On a `uses` step it must map `Unreachable`.

effect.description: One thing an alternative ending does instead of the main path (Section 3.3): a single step verb, without `becomes`.

uses.description: A Function of another Component, as "Interface / Function".

alternative.description: A non-main ending of a Function (Section 3.3): one plain-language sentence saying what happened — it leaves nothing changed — or, when the ending does something, `when` plus `effects`.

callerKey.description: The caller an Interface serves: the name of an Actor, or the reserved key `Components` for Functions of other Components (Section 3.3). That an Actor name refers to an existing Actor is checked outside JSON Schema.

response.description: What a caller gets back for one outcome (Section 3.3): a code alone, or a code and a body. Code values are defined by the contract's binding.

exposure.description: How one Function is reached through an Interface (Section 3.3).

operation.description: What the caller invokes, in the style's own terms (e.g. "GET /{id}", "GetOrder"); format defined by the binding.

request.description: What the caller sends, in the core type notation. It may reference the Component's own Data Objects, nested types and projections only.

responses.description: Every outcome of the Function — its result and each alternative — mapped to what the caller gets back. Coverage is checked outside JSON Schema.

style.description: The style whose binding interprets every other key in this block (e.g. OpenAPI, gRPC, MCP, Web UI).

binding.description: The Interface's technology (Section 3.3). Contour defines only `style`; every other key is defined by that style's binding.

exposes.description: The Component's Functions this Interface makes reachable: keyed by Function name with operation, request and responses, or — for a binding whose conventions cover them, such as a Web UI — a plain list of Function names.

interface.description: An Interface (Section 3): a channel on its Component's boundary through which one caller reaches the Component. A Function is external exactly when some Interface exposes it.

groups.description: The Components this System groups, nested as full element objects (ownership by nesting).

interfaces.description: The Interfaces this Component provides, nested; each serves one caller.

functions.description: The Functions this Component performs, nested (ownership by nesting).

dataObjects.description: The Data Objects this Component owns and keeps, nested. Data that only crosses a boundary is described in a contract instead.

events.description: The Events this Component produces, nested. An Event this Component only reacts to is referenced by name via `consumes`, not nested (it is owned by the producing Component).

references.description: Names of Data Objects owned by another Component that this Component reads/references (Context-view resolution).

consumes.description: Names of Events produced by another Component that this Component reacts to — a Context-view summary of its Functions' `consumes` first steps (Section 3.4).

dependsOn.description: Names of Components this Component depends on — a Context-view summary of its Functions' `uses` steps (Section 3.2).

steps.description: The main path, in order (Section 3.3). The diagram's edges for these verbs are a derived summary of it.

result.description: The name of the ending the main path reaches.

alternatives.description: Every other way the Function can end, keyed by outcome name.

behavior.description: Business rules the steps and endings don't express.

function.description: A Function (Section 3), in business terms only. It is external when an Interface of its Component exposes it, private otherwise; it declares no inputs and carries nothing technical.

name.description: Event name, in the past tense (Section 3.5), e.g. "Order Placed".

definition.description: A record-tier Requirement or Guardrail definition (Section 3.6): a name and a description, referenced by name from the elements it applies to. Never drawn as a diagram element.
